key_insight: LongAgent turns longitudinal prediction into a history-guided agentic search problem, helping the model focus on the most informative patient variables over time. This makes it easier to predict future outcomes from messy, heterogeneous medical records.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of learning useful predictive representations from longitudinal medical data that are heterogeneous, irregularly sampled, and spread across many variables and sources.
method: Uses an agentic search strategy to identify variables and temporal signals that are most relevant for outcome prediction.
Guides the search with patient history so the model can selectively process longitudinal information instead of treating all measurements equally.
Integrates information across multiple variables and time points to build a more predictive representation of health trajectories.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners in healthcare, this offers a more targeted way to handle noisy, sparse, and irregular time-series data. It can improve prediction quality while reducing the burden of manually selecting features from complex clinical records.
visual_elements: Timeline of patient records showing irregular visits, labs, and events

paper_title: LongAgent: History-Guided Agentic Search for Longitudinal Outcome Prediction
paper_authors: Siyao Wang, Florian Guitton, Shuojie Fu, Guanyu Tao, Kai Sun
